approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create a licensing system for building, running and removing offshore electricity equipment in Australian waters.
The minister would decide which areas are open for projects and grant permits, while new statutory bodies would oversee the scheme.
Work health and safety rules under the Work Health and Safety Act 2011 would apply to these offshore activities, with modifications.
Makes it illegal to carry out offshore electricity activities without a licence.
Lets the minister declare zones where offshore electricity work can happen.
Gives the minister power to issue licences for projects in those zones.
Protects offshore electricity infrastructure in Commonwealth waters.
Sets up official bodies to run and enforce the new framework.
Applies modified workplace safety laws to offshore electricity operations.
Companies and investors wanting to build offshore electricity projects in Commonwealth waters, plus existing marine users who must be consulted.

The Morrison government introduced the Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill to establish a regulatory framework for offshore electricity projects, citing specific proposals like Marinus Link, Star of the South, and Sun Cable, which are estimated to be worth over $10 billion and create over 10,000 jobs during construction.

The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure (Regulatory Levies) Bill 2021 was introduced to ensure full cost recovery for the Offshore Infrastructure Registrar and Regulator, with NOPTA and NOPSEMA appointed to administer and regulate the framework, supporting the development of offshore electricity projects.

The Labor Party supported the Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill 2021 as overdue, citing offshore wind's potential for jobs and energy export, but criticised the government for ignoring bipartisan recommendations on work health and safety harmonisation and local community benefits, moving a second reading amendment to address these issues.

The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill 2021 was argued to enable offshore renewable energy, with the three most advanced projects—Star of the South, Marinus Link, and Sun Cable—potentially delivering $10 billion in investment and over 10,000 jobs during construction.

The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill 2021 was argued to be essential for enabling major renewable projects like Marinus Link, Star of the South, and Sun Cable, while protecting maritime stakeholders and the environment. The speech also reaffirmed the Morrison government's net zero emissions by 2050 target and its technology-focused plan to reduce emissions.

The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill 2021 was argued as essential for enabling Australia’s offshore wind potential and grid-stabilising projects like Marinus Link, Star of the South and Sun Cable, while the government announced a net zero by 2050 target backed by a Long Term Emissions Reduction Plan, noting Australia’s 20.8% emissions reduction since 2005.

The Offshore Electricity Infrastructure Bill 2021 requires improvements in work health and safety harmonisation, a clear process for declaring offshore areas, and legislated merit criteria for local and environmental benefits.
